digest.en: China pulled out of a Sri Lankan port logistics venture while a Russian satellite flew dangerously close to Ukrainian assets. ASEAN quietly prepares for the next regional disaster as funding cuts leave half a million people without food assistance.
digest.hi: यमन में हूती मिसाइलों ने सैन्य शिविर पर हमला किया जिसमें 53 सैनिक मारे गए। इसी वक्त फ्रांस से अल्बानिया तक आगजनी और जनाक्रोश ने यूरोप में नया तनाव पैदा किया है।

articles.title: ASEAN’s quiet work before the next deadly disaster
articles.summary: ASEAN officials highlight the bloc's behind-the-scenes disaster preparedness efforts. This work often goes unnoticed compared to its political failures. The authors argue this quiet coordination is critical for regional resilience. ASEAN often gets criticised for the political crises it cannot resolve. The work it puts into preparing for major disasters is less visible, say Lim Junli and Ian Li from the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies.

articles.title: Saudi envoy meets Pakistan Army chief, discusses regional security dynamics
articles.summary: A Saudi envoy met the Pakistan Army chief in Rawalpindi. They reviewed progress under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. Both sides emphasized strengthening defense collaboration and strategic coordination for regional security. During the meeting at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, both sides expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination, the army said in a statement.

articles.title: Donald Trump rallies on Republican turf as midterm fears mount
articles.summary: Donald Trump held a rally near Wichita with 15 days left in the election. He aimed to support Senator Roger Marshall. Marshall is tied with a Methodist pastor in a tight race for the Senate seat. With 15 days until the November 3 vote, Donald Trump’s rally on the outskirts of Wichita aims to shore up Senator Roger Marshall, who is locked in a dead heat with a Methodist megachurch pastor.

articles.title: A growing national crisis and a strategic warning
articles.summary: South Korea's per capita GDP is projected to surpass Japan's by 2027. The International Monetary Fund estimates Korea will reach $49,000. Japan is expected to sit between $37,000 and $38,000. This shift highlights Korea's semiconductor strength. Recent media reports projecting South Korea’s per capita GDP to surpass Japan’s have generated considerable excitement across the regional countries that see Korea as a role model.

articles.title: China pulls out of key investment in Sri Lanka port logistics venture
articles.summary: China Merchants withdrew its investment from a Sri Lankan port logistics venture. The 2023 pledge was the first major foreign direct investment after Sri Lanka's debt default. The pullback signals reduced Chinese commitment to the island's infrastructure recovery. When China Merchants pledged the investment in 2023, it was touted as the “first major Foreign Direct Investment” to enter Sri Lanka after the country defaulted on its foreign debt the previous year amid a crushing economic crisis.

articles.title: A Russian Military Satellite Gets Very, Very Close To One Used By Ukraine
articles.summary: A Russian military satellite passed exceptionally close to a Finnish-operated satellite. The Finnish satellite provides intelligence to Ukraine. Officials described the maneuver as concerning and aggressive. They noted it may serve as a signal of hostile intent. Last week, a Russian military satellite came “exceptionally close” to another Finnish-operated satellite that provides intelligence to Ukraine. “It’s concerning and aggressive with potential hostile intent – but I also think cooler heads believe it is signaling on the part of the Russians.”.

articles.title: A Warm Welcome for US Secretary of State in Central Asia
articles.summary: U. S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to Central Asia. The region offered a warm welcome to the Trump administration. This trip allowed Rubio to bypass other pressing international crises. The visit secured diplomatic goodwill in the area. Not only can Rubio avoid the most pressing international crises by jetting off to Central Asia, but he – and the Trump administration more broadly – were guaranteed to receive a warm welcome in the region.

articles.title: 'We're Never Going To Be The Major Player': Former Diplomat's Reality Check On US Ambitions In
articles.summary: Daniel Rosenblum, a former US ambassador, warns that American business efforts in Central Asia face significant hurdles. He argues the United States will not become a major regional player despite recent diplomatic outreach. Marco Rubio has brought nearly 300 American business representatives to Uzbekistan for a meeting with representatives of the five states of Central Asia. But Daniel N. Rosenblum, a former US ambassador to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, cautions that investment faces major obstacles.

articles.title: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
articles.summary: The World Food Programme cut Gaza aid by one third due to funding shortages. The reduction leaves roughly 500,000 people without food assistance as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday. Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

articles.title: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres honored four Indonesian peacekeepers killed in Lebanon. He laid a wreath in their memory and defended the organization's peacekeeping mission during what he described as testing times for global stability. UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

articles.title: Owner or owned? Indonesia’s Chinese battery chain dilemma
articles.summary: Indonesia seeks to transform raw nickel exports into high-value EV batteries. The strategy relies heavily on Chinese investment and technology, raising questions about whether Indonesia controls its supply chain or remains dependent on foreign partners. Indonesia has spent a decade trying to turn its mineral wealth into something more valuable than raw commodity exports. The strategy is ambitious: restrict raw nickel exports, attract investment, build processing capacity and move downstream into electric-vehicle (EV) batteries that will power the next generation of transport and energy storage.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary: Hurricane Trudy weakened to a tropical storm after threatening Mexico's Pacific coast. The system remained 160 kilometers southwest of the shore. Meanwhile, deadly floods in Greece killed one person. The Pacific season saw 22 named systems this year. Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in GreeceIn contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system.

articles.title: Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia
articles.summary: Marco Rubio stated the United States will continue pushing for a Ukraine peace deal. He warned the conflict risks escalating beyond Russia and Ukraine. The Secretary of State made these remarks while meeting Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would continue efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine, warning that the conflict risks escalating beyond the two countries as he met with Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan.

articles.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
articles.summary: China's third-quarter GDP grew by 4.5 percent year-on-year. The figure exceeded previous forecasts. Strong electronics demand boosted industrial output and exports. Factory growth significantly outpaced consumer spending during the July to September period. Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demandBusiness live – latest updatesRoaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending. China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on.

articles.title: Strategy trumps scandal as West goes easy on India
articles.summary: Canada and India reaffirmed plans to expand trade and security cooperation on October 13. This move occurred despite ongoing Western accusations of Indian foreign interference and intelligence operations. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Prime Minister Narendra Modi prioritized strategic alignment over diplomatic friction. The decision signals that geopolitical utility outweighs security concerns for Western partners. Western governments are rebuilding ties with India even as they accuse it of foreign interference and of running intelligence operations against people on their soil.

articles.title: What Australia could learn from SE Asia about managing China
articles.summary: Australian governments have tightened foreign interference laws to counter Chinese influence. They also regulated university collaborations and foreign investment. Officials launched a Pacific Step-Up plan. These measures aim to strengthen trade ties with Southeast Asia. Successive Australian governments have reacted with alarm at China’s influence-building activities in Southeast Asia and the Pacific. They have passed foreign interference laws, tightened foreign investment regulations, and regulated university collaborations with institutions overseas.

articles.title: Trump Says Zelenskyy Should 'Get Somebody Else To Negotiate'
articles.summary: Donald Trump defended waiving planned sanctions against Russia to maintain negotiations. Kyiv and some US lawmakers criticized the move. They argued it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin. The decision drew strong opposition from allies. President Donald Trump defended his decision to waive sweeping sanctions planned against Russia as an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table amid strong criticism from Kyiv and some US lawmakers that it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin.

articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
articles.summary: Argentina’s president is targeting the Falklands’ oil and fisheries industries amid declining poll numbers. Local residents and military police gathered in the islands’ legislative assembly. The move signals renewed hostility toward the British territory after four decades. Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly.

articles.title: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule
articles.summary: Garry Kasparov told RFE/RL that talks with Putin are pointless. He believes the war is the ideological basis of Putin's rule. Kasparov criticized a proposed US deal to buy Russian diesel. He argued Ukraine's victory would force Putin's fall. Russian Chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov tells RFE/RL Putin is set on “liquidating Ukraine” and will not concessions. Slamming a proposed US deal to buy Russian diesel, Kasparov said that if Ukraine wins the war Putin will fall – giving a chance for democracy in Russia.

articles.title: Flour sacks turned flood barriers: Gaza faces another winter without safe shelter
articles.summary: Families in the Gaza Strip are bracing for a winter of severe cold and rain that threatens to flood their remaining shelters. Ahmed Al-Omari and others are repurposing flour sacks as makeshift barriers against rising water. These improvised defenses highlight the lack of safe, durable housing in the war-ravaged territory. Residents continue to live in tattered tents and damaged buildings with no reliable protection from the elements. The situation underscores the ongoing humanitarian crisis as winter approaches.

articles.title: Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions
articles.summary: Russia fired missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities on 17 October, killing at least twelve civilians and damaging residential blocks and power infrastructure. Russia continued to pound Ukraine with missiles and drones, killing civilians and damaging residential buildings and energy sites, as Kyiv described disruptions to the satellite communications of US company SpaceX, crucial to the country's defense, as a deliberate "operation.".

articles.title: Sanctions, War, Isolation: Why Hasn't Iran's Hard-Line Government Collapsed?
articles.summary: Iran's government has survived war, economic crisis, and mass protests. Vahid Pourostad attributes this resilience to entrenched power networks. The opposition remains fractured and unable to mount a unified challenge. The Islamic republic continues to hold power despite severe internal and external pressure. Iran’s Islamic republic has survived war, economic crisis, and widespread protests. So why is the system still standing?

articles.title: Trump Waives Graham Act Sanctions On Russia Before They Take Effect
articles.summary: Trump waived nearly all sanctions from the Graham Act before they took effect. The bipartisan law aimed to pressure Russia to end its war against Ukraine. The move prompted sharp criticism from Ukraine advocates. Lawmakers from both parties in the US condemned the decision. US President Donald Trump has waived nearly all substantive sanctions, tariffs, and restrictions included in a bipartisan law aimed at pressuring Russia to end its war against Ukraine, prompting sharp criticism from Ukraine advocates and US lawmakers from both parties.

articles.title: China, Russia quietly moving toward a new Arctic axis
articles.summary: Putin’s advisor Nikolai Patrushev visited China to advance Arctic cooperation. The talks focused on converting maritime agreements into durable infrastructure and logistics. This shift aims to build a resilient axis that can withstand ongoing geopolitical pressure. Russian President Vladimir Putin’s advisor Nikolai Patrushev’s recent visit to China points to something more consequential than another round of Russia-China strategic rhetoric: Moscow is trying to turn maritime cooperation with Beijing into infrastructure, technology and logistics that can survive geopolitical pressure.

articles.title: Can a cockroach movement reverse India’s democratic decline?
articles.summary: India deployed over 25,000 police officers in New Delhi to stop Cockroach Janta Party protests. Authorities denied the youth-led group permission to demonstrate, citing public order concerns. The security operation resulted in the closure of one in six metro stations. More than 25,000 police officers were deployed across New Delhi recently to prevent demonstrations led by India’s new youth-led political movement, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

articles.summary: ईरान ने होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में बढ़ते तनाव के लिए अमेरिका को ज़िम्मेदार ठहराया। ट्रंप ने इस जलमार्ग को अपने नाम पर बुलाकर अमेरिकी नियंत्रण का दावा किया। ईरान ने इस दावे को खारिज करते हुए क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा के लिए अमेरिकी हस्तक्षेप को मुख्य कारण बताया। इस रणनीतिक जलमार्ग पर हमेशा से ही ईरान का कंट्रोल रहा है, लेकिन अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप (Donald Trump) पिछले कुछ समय से इसे ‘ट्रंप स्ट्रेट’ (Strait of Trump) बता रहे हैं और दावा कर रहे हैं कि इस पर अमेरिकी नेवी का कंट्रोल है।

articles.summary: शबवा प्रांत में हूती विद्रोहियों ने बैलिस्टिक मिसाइलों से सैनिक ट्रेनिंग कैंप पर हमला किया। यमन सरकार ने 20 सैनिकों की मौत की पुष्टि की है। कम से कम दो दर्जन सैनिक घायल हुए हैं। शबवा प्रांत में यमन की सरकार ने मिलिट्री ट्रेनिंग कैंप पर हूतियों के बैलिस्टिक मिसाइल हमले में 20 लड़ाकों के मारे जाने की पुष्टी की है.

articles.title: कांग्रेस का असदुद्दीन ओवैसी पर बड़ा आरोप, कहा- ‘वे भारत के अंदर...’
articles.summary: कांग्रेस ने असदुद्दीन ओवैसी की रामपुर में की गई टिप्पणी पर नाराजगी जताई है। पार्टी प्रवक्ता शमा मोहम्मद ने ओवैसी की बातों की आलोचना की है। यह बयान उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव के बीच आया है। उत्तर प्रदेश में होने वाले विधानसभा चुनाव को लेकर AIMIM प्रमुख असदुद्दीन ओवैसी राज्य भर में घूम-घूमकर रैलियां और जनसभाएं कर रहे हैं. इसी कड़ी में असदुद्दीन ओवैसी ने यूपी के रामपुर में आयोजित एक जनसभा को संबोधित करते हुए कुछ ऐसी टिप्पणी की, जिसपर देश की मुख्य विपक्षी पार्टी कांग्रेस ने नाराजगी जताई है.
